response.query: Which causal-identification approach (difference-in-differences, synthetic control, interrupted time series or matched comparisons) best suits our policy exposures, and what pre-specified assumptions, placebo tests and pre-treatment trend diagnostics are needed?
response.answer: Interrupted time series is often best for policy exposures, assuming stable pre-treatment trends. Use placebo tests and pre-treatment trend diagnostics to validate assumptions. Difference-in-differences and matched comparisons can also be effective depending on context.
